segments.text: [Music]
Hey fellow
developers, are you still stuck using
the HTTP package for API calls? You're
about to discover something way more
powerful. Dio, the ultimate networking
tool for Flutter. It makes your API
logic cleaner, smarter, and easier to
scale. The HTTP package is fine for
small projects, but it's very basic. You
can't easily add global headers. There's
no built-in support for interceptors,
token refresh, retries, or logging. All
of which are essential in real world
apps. It quickly becomes repetitive and
messy as your project
grows. That's where Dio comes in. It
offers interceptors for headers and
logging, built-in retry and timeout
control, cleaner error responses, token
refresh support, perform data handling,
much more scalable and developer
friendly. To install Dio, just add this
package to your project. Get and post
requests. Here's a simple do get request
and IO post request with headers.
Dio makes it easy to add O tokens, show
loaders, refresh tokens, and more using
interceptors. No need to repeat the same
logic in every request. Error handling
and logging. With Dio, you get
structured error handling using Dio
error, and you can easily plug in
logging with log interceptor. Debugging
becomes super easy. Dio also supports
cancel tokens, file uploads, timeouts,
custom adapters, and more, making it
perfect for complex and production grade
apps. When to use Dio? If you're
building anything beyond a basic
prototype, Dio will save you time in
code. It's a mustave for serious Flutter
apps. If you found this helpful, don't
forget to like the video. Subscribe for
more Flutter tips, tricks, and
tutorials. Let me know in the comments.
Are you already using Dio or thinking
about making the switch? I'd love to
hear your experience. Thanks for
watching, and as always, happy coding.
